title: OMTM and North Star Metrics Without Tunnel Vision
editorial_note: Opening revised to lead with the lesson itself. Remaining dialogue is an automated editorial draft; review spoken wording and meaning before final publication.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: OMTM and North Star Metrics Without Tunnel Vision.

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: The OMTM is stage- and problem-specific. It asks: what single measure best tells this team whether it is overcoming the constraint that matters now? During problem discovery it might be evidence of need; during activation it might be meaningful first success; during retention it might be repeated value. It should change when the constraint changes.

turns.speaker: host
turns.act: OMTM and North Star serve different horizons
turns.text: What changes when we look at omtm and north star serve different horizons?

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: A North Star metric is more durable. It represents the recurring event or result in which customers receive core value and the product creates sustainable value. It is not simply revenue, users, clicks, or transactions. A useful North Star has a clear value event, qualifying conditions, actor, frequency, and connection to strategy.

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Focus measures sit inside an architecture. Input metrics reveal levers; diagnostics explain movement; guardrails protect quality and stakeholders; outcomes validate whether the focus still predicts value.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What changes when we look at test a candidate focus metric?

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Ask:

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Does the unit represent delivered value rather than activity or availability? Can teams influence it through legitimate product and service improvements? Is it sensitive enough to guide current decisions? Does it have a plausible relationship to durable user and organisational value? Can it be defined consistently and audited? How can it be gamed?

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Which people, contexts, or sides of the system can it sacrifice? What metric should replace it when the constraint changes?

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Use a “perverse design” exercise: deliberately invent ways to increase the metric while harming users. Those examples expose missing qualifying conditions and guardrails.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What changes when we look at transfer example: language learning?

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: “Lessons completed” can be increased with shorter lessons and pressure notifications. “Learners who successfully practise and return at an appropriate cadence” is closer to recurring value, but still needs comprehension, frustration, accessibility, and notification guardrails.

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: During early activation work, the OMTM might be target learners reaching one meaningful first success; later it may shift to sustained practice.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What changes when we look at multi-sided systems need balance?

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Marketplaces, care services, and platforms create value through several actors. Orders can grow while suppliers are overwhelmed; patient bookings can rise while clinic rejection climbs. Avoid averaging unlike value into an opaque composite. Use a clear focus measure with participant-balance diagnostics and veto guardrails.

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: If one side’s capacity is the constraint, the OMTM may intentionally focus there for a period.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What changes when we look at where this can go wrong?

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Vanity North Star: a large cumulative total feels impressive but guides no value decision. Permanent OMTM: yesterday’s constraint governs today’s work. Metric monoculture: guardrails and qualitative evidence lose authority. Goodhart capture: teams learn to increase the number without the construct.

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: One-sided value: customers improve by extracting unsustainable labour from partners or staff. Average blindness: growth in one segment conceals exclusion elsewhere.

turns.speaker: host
turns.act: Define focus with an expiry and guardrails
turns.text: What changes when we look at define focus with an expiry and guardrails?

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: The team may temporarily focus on clinic acknowledgement for valid transfers because the service blueprint identifies an unowned handoff. The metric has an expiry condition: once reliability reaches the agreed level, focus shifts to the next constraint.

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Outcome and guardrails remain visible throughout, including unsuitable acceptance, original-slot loss, unequal delay, and coordinator burden.

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Targets use baseline, uncertainty, capacity, and expected mechanism. They are not motivational numbers chosen by leadership. Review asks why the metric moved and whether the behaviour it encouraged still serves the outcome. Teams can stop using an OMTM that has become a gaming target or no longer represents the bottleneck.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What changes when we look at transfer example: marketplace?

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Completed transactions can be a North Star only if they represent genuine buyer and seller value. Fraud, cancellation, dispute, delivery failure, and seller sustainability prevent the number from becoming a tunnel-vision target.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Where does the harder design decision appear?

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Focus is an allocation decision. Senior practitioners explain why this constraint matters now, what work it displaces, and when focus ends. They do not cascade the North Star into individual performance targets; that invites local gaming. They review the metric whenever teams discover a reliable way to move it without improving the underlying outcome.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What changes when we look at focus attention without collapsing value?

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: The metric definition includes eligible population, quality threshold, time, and guardrails. The team identifies how it could be gamed—for example, accepting only easy cases—and reviews a balanced scorecard. Focus helps coordination only when the omitted dimensions remain protected.

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: <! -- Editorial: manual revision; curated product example --

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Can we see that in a concrete product situation?

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Illustrative scenario: a marketplace. A north-star measure of completed, trusted transactions may align teams better than page views. But one number cannot represent seller fairness, dispute resolution, or people excluded before purchase. The team pairs its focus measure with guardrails and revisits it when incentives cause gaming.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What should I notice the next time I use a product?

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Infer the North Star of a product from its interface and notifications. What behaviour is it encouraging? Name one stakeholder or quality the apparent metric could make invisible.
